verdicts.working: Molecule: OHC–CHCl–CH(OH)–CH3. Take I = C2 (Cl-bearing), II = C3 (OH-bearing) per IUPAC numbering. Applying Fischer convention (near-horizontal bonds toward viewer, near-vertical away; implicit H away): C-I priorities Cl > CHO [(O,O,H)] > CH(OH)CH3 [(O,C,H)] > H; with H back, Cl(top)→CHO(lower-left)→C3(lower-right) is counterclockwise = S. C-II priorities OH > CHCl– [(Cl,C,H)] > CH3 > H; OH(bottom)→C2(upper-left)→CH3(upper-right) is clockwise = R. Hence I: S, II: R.
issues: Figure is a bent zigzag skeletal drawing, not a standard Fischer projection (no vertical backbone/crosses); configurations are only assignable by assuming the Fischer convention (horizontal = front, vertical = back) stated in the text — as an ordinary flat skeletal structure it carries no stereochemical information.

Stereocentres are not labelled I and II in the figure; assignment relies on the natural IUPAC numbering (I = C2 bearing Cl, II = C3 bearing OH). If the labels were intended the other way, option B would result.
Hydrogens on the stereocentres are implicit, which is unusual for a Fischer projection where all four groups are normally shown.

working:
At I: Cl $>$ CHO $>$ C(OH)(H)CH$_3$ $>$ H; $1\to2\to3$ is clockwise, and horizontal H requires inversion: S.
At II: OH $>$ C(Cl)(H)CHO $>$ CH$_3$ $>$ H; $1\to2\to3$ is clockwise, and horizontal H requires inversion: S.
solution:
At I, the priority order is Cl $>$ CHO $>$ C(OH)(H)CH$_3$ $>$ H. The $1\to2\to3$ order is clockwise, but horizontal H points forward, so inversion gives $S$.
At II, OH $>$ C(Cl)(H)CHO $>$ CH$_3$ $>$ H; the clockwise order is likewise inverted because H is horizontal, giving $S$.
